novel_mechanics_found: Level 3 adds a brown-headed, vertically connected colored chain that is absent from level 2. ACTION1/2 move the left head by one six-pixel lattice row, while ACTION3/4 retract or retain horizontal chain segments. Touching the connected chain at E couples the objects: a subsequent downward move drags the entire brown-headed colored chain down one lattice row. Direct ACTION6 clicks on the brown head and bottom reference head produced no visible effect.
narrative: The verified 44-action prefix reached levels_completed=2 both live and through the mandatory fresh-reset reproduction gate. I explored level 3 by comparing its rendered layout with the known L1/L2 routes, testing retained-segment color visitation in the bottom reference order and in the connected-chain reverse order from fresh prefix replays. Those candidates did not level up; the important new behavior was physical coupling and whole-chain dragging after contact with the previously unexplained brown-headed chain. I stopped at the verified L2 ceiling with 20 steps remaining because another fresh L3 candidate plus its reproduction gate could not fit within the 600-step budget.
gotchas: A horizontal color contact is not enough by itself: retracting all the way discards the useful retained-chain configuration; L1/L2 retain one or more segments between row changes.
Level 3's brown 2x2 head and its 2/3 connector glyphs are functional: contact can couple the movable chain to the whole vertical colored chain, which then moves as a unit.

Calling env.reset() after reaching level 3 returned a frame still reporting levels_completed=2, but the next action could drop the run to level 0; use a fresh environment plus the full verified prefix for trustworthy L3 trials.
ACTION6 clicks at visible head coordinates were frame-identical no-ops in the tested states.
The stable rendered grid is the last item of frame.frame; individual actions can contain multiple animation frames.
